description.narrative: Center for Human Rights (CHR) etablerades 2008 som en självständig akademisk enhet inom Addis Ababa Universitetet (AAU). Centret engagerar sig i multi-disciplinärt Mänsklig Rättighetsarbete inom bl.a. undervisning, forskning och arbete med bl.a. rättshjälp till behövande grupper i samhället. I enlighet med AAU och CHRs 10-års plan avser centret bli ett av Afrikas ledande forskningsinstitut till år 2030. CHR har 12 anställda akademiker, varav de flesta doktorerade. Projektet har tre övergripande målsättningar: 1) Statliga funktioner har stärkt sin kapacitet att respektera de mänskliga rättigheterna och skydda kvinnor, barn, funktionsvarierade, arbetares och migranters rättigheter. 2) Civilsamhällesorganisationer har stärkts i sin roll att främja de mänskliga rättigheterna och i att skydda ovan grupper i samhället. 3) Kvinnor, barn funktionsvarierade, arbetares och migranters mänskliga rättigheter har skyddat

The CHR was founded in 2008 and is a semi-autonomous institution part of the College of Law and Governance Studies - at Addis Ababa University (AAU). The mission of CHR is to promote human rights through multidisciplinary teaching and training, research, and community service. According to the AAU and CHR’s 10-year plan, the centre aspires to be the leading Human Rights Research Centre in Africa by 2030. CHR has 12 employees, most of who are PhD holders. CHR-STRACE II, has three main objectives: i) increase the capacity of state agencies to respect human rights and to protect the rights of women, children, persons with disabilities, workers, and migrants ii) Empower civil society organizations to be active actors in human rights promotion and in protecting the rights of women, children, persons with disabilities, workers, and migrants; and iii) better protect the rights of women, children, persons with disabilities, workers, and migrants.

The overarching aim of the project is to ensure the respect of all human rights of all Ethiopians. Project set three interrelated goals: i) Increase the capacity of state agencies to respect human rights and to protect the rights of women, children, persons with disabilities, workers and migrants ii) Empower civil society organizations to be active actors in human rights promotion and in protecting the rights of women, children, persons with disabilities, workers, and migrants; and iii) Better protect the rights of women, children, persons with disabilities, workers and migrants. To contribute to the realization of these goals, the Project will carry out activities that are grouped under three Sub-Projects: a) Multidisciplinary Human Rights Teaching and Training; b) Research, Policy and Practice Collaboration and Diffusion; 3) Community Based Human Rights Promotion and Protection.
The activities in the project includes: i) launching of one new graduate level human rights education program, provide short term specialized training on human rights ii) review existing MA and Ph.D Program iii) produce textbooks for the multidisciplinary teaching of human rights, iv) organize academic conferences, organize policy dialogue forums, promote the multidisciplinary engagement of human rights, train and support community based organizations to engage in human rights promotion and protection, and v) provide legal and related services to members of disadvantaged social groups

title.narrative: Centre for Human Rights STRACE II project
Centre for Human Rights STRACE II project

description.narrative:
The main achievement for this reporting period was the successful completion of the inception phase of the project, see inception report for detailed results. During this phase, the RBM was updated, and results matrix developed.
The project has three main areas or sub-projects; i) Multidisciplinary Human Rights Teaching and Training ii) Research, Policy and Practice Collaboration and Diffusion iii) Community Based Human Rights Promotion and Protection
i) Multidisciplinary Human Rights Teaching and Training
This sub project focuses on promoting human rights through teaching and training programs that includes MA and PhD programs in Human Rights and MA program in Childrens Rights Studies. The main achievement was a five-day training was conducted from November 18 to 22 at a post graduate level for high and mid-level government officials and CSO leaders on Human Rights and Media Freedom. This theme was in line with the ongoing national policy dialogues on transitional justice process. The focus was laid on contributions and the role of digital technology in the ongoing transitional justice process of the nation. Hence, the training on media freedom and human rights was carried out to enhance knowledge of media personnel/outlets, advocates, defenders, relevant government institutions and CSOs with the central focus of ensuring the promotion and protection of human rights.
The training was well attended by, among others, Ethiopia Media Authority and the Federal Police Commission as well as regional participants from Benishangul Gumuz, Oromia, Harari, Dire Dawa, Afar, and SNNPR. Participants gave positive review, at the end of the training.
As part of mainstreaming human rights at AAU, 20 students were trained as ToT in Human Rights Education, who in turned facilitated the training of 500 undergraduate students.
In addition, a new module to address the human rights of vulnerable communities at times of conflict under the topic Human Right under Conflict Situations: The Nexus between Peace and Human Rights".
NOTE: Two planned activities; hosting of an international researcher and developing curriculum for human rights post-graduate course were not realised. The latter due to new government directive to halt development of new programmes in the universities, until further notice.
ii) Research, Policy and Practice Collaboration and Diffusion
This sub-project focus on promoting policy discussions and dialogue informed by human rights-based approach, create shared understanding, and facilitate common action against human rights violations by state and non-state actors, and improve the availability of empirical academic resources and publications on human rights protection in Ethiopia.
CHR plan to organize a policy dialogue on "Socio economic rights of citizens on the first year of the project, was changed to transitional justice to adapt to the socio-political context and contribute to the ongoing national dialogues on transitional justice. Communication materials were developed in collaboration with experts on transitional justice in AAU. A policy dialogue forum on Contributions of the Academia to the Transitional Justice Policy Options for Ethiopia'' was organised in October 2023, targeting experts on transitional justice who were selected primarily from different academic and research institutions in Ethiopia.
ii) Community Based Human Rights Promotion and Protection
A total of 73 (36 F and 37M) members of local community-based associations, completed training as Community Right Promoters (CRP). The training focused on trainees understanding of basic human rights of women, children, PWDs and workers. The CRP training has laid the foundation for improved engagements of Community Based Organizations (CBOs) to promote the rights of vulnerable groups and contribute towards improved human rights knowledge, attitude, and practice at community level. Ten CRPs were retained for public awareness raising at each Project Area.
A total of 117 government officials (55 female and 62 Male) consisting of local government officials serving Womens and Social Affairs Offices, police departments, Bureau of Labor and Skills, Peace and Security Offices, courts and social workers were offered training on womens rights, childrens rights, workers rights, and rights of persons with disabilities. The training was conducted in Addis Ababa, Hawassa, Debre Berhan, Adama and Ambo in November 2023.
CHR trained 60 paralegals (30M, 30F) in May 2023. The trainings were held in Debre Berhan, Ambo and Addis Ababa. A total of 5725 (3301F and 2424M) benefitted from paralegal support during the reporting period in Ambo. Adama. Addis Ababa, Debre Berhan and Hawassa.
CHR set up a Local Advisory Committee (LAC) comprising of 10 active Community Right Promoters (CRPs) and 25 representatives from key stakeholder groups, including courts, women's and children's affairs offices, police, and civil society organizations. Adapting a participatory and co-creation approach to the project management has improved the project governance which will ultimately contribute to sustainability of the structures created in the project areas, beyond the end of the project period.
